header_changes_needed: none for vec3.h / albw_types.h: Vec3 copy-initialisation from a global const Vec3 reproduces the target's ldm/stm block copies (0x4FD538 etc.) unchanged

not a shared-header change but a finding for other enemy ctors: the nothrow tag type must be 1 byte with a user-declared ctor (struct NoThrow { NoThrow() {} u8 pad; }). A 4-byte tag makes armcc spill the tag to the stack (str r5,[sp] + ldr r1,[sp] before every operator new); an empty tag passes no r1 at all. Only the 1-byte form gives the target's plain `mov r1, r5` (0x4FD4A0/0x4FD4C0/0x4FD4E8/0x4FD620).

StateMgr note from the coordinator (names at +0x08/+0x0C are a Buffer of FixedSafeString<24>) does not affect this function: EnemyBase's ctor never touches a StateMgr (derived ctors place it at +0x8BC).
new_types: logs/manual/H_004FD464/actor_types.h -- ActorBaseA/ActorBaseB/ActorBase (0x40C, 21 primary slots, ctor 0x150E40, members m2d0/m3a4/m3cc/m3ec); Obj2D0 (m18 sub-object, m1c8[] u32 array); EnemyParam (flags m0, m4, m8, mC, m10, m18, m44); E00E (12-byte {u32,u8,f32}, ctor 0x4FD414); H00E (4-byte, ctor 0x4FC988); S00E (16-byte {f32,Vec3}, ctor 0x4F7DFC); Dlg (16-byte {vptr, object, PMF}, vtable ro_006F4C98, PMF table ro_0069512C); Sub5A8 (0xB0-byte sub-object at +0x5A8: E00E[7], void*[7], H00E[7], H00E[7], counts at +0xA8..+0xAB, 0xA/0xA at +0xAC/+0xAD, inline addUnique); A03E/Sub658 (20 x {u32,u32,f32} = {0,0,1.0f} at +0x658); Sub748 (2 x S00E at +0x748); X00E/X10E/X20E/X30E (heap members 0x64/0x0C/0x48/0x2C4, ctors 0x4EE484/0x32493C/0x34CAA0/0x2B2590); EnemyBase itself (sizeof == 0x8BC verified by compiling sizeof(EnemyBase); 0x8BC bytes, 31 primary vtable slots, secondary vptr at +0x320 = vtable+0x84, every member offset documented with the instruction that initialises it).
blocker: Register allocation, not structure. 338 of the 596 instructions (56.7%) already match modulo register names and the stream is aligned end to end (581 vs 596 words); the exact-word count is dominated by one allocator decision. The target keeps the zero constant in fp (r11) and reloads the rodata PMF base into r1 as a scratch; armcc 4.1 puts the zero constant in sb (r9) and hoists the PMF base into fp across the delegate block, which renames ~150 stores and changes the delegate store grouping (target: mObj, PMF, then vptr; mine: vptr+mObj merged into one stm). The PMF base is hoisted because the null PMF constant and the m554 PMF constant end up adjacent in my rodata, so the compiler derives both from one base; in the target they are 0x40 apart (0x69517C vs 0x69513C) and are loaded as two independent symbols. Second: the stack frame is 0x14 instead of 0xC because the flags byte handed to func_004FC798 (0x4FDC08 strb r0,[sp]; 0x4FDC10 mov r2,sp) is a local in my source and armcc gives it its own slot above the 12-byte outgoing-argument area, whereas the target's byte lives inside that area; every shape I tried (u8 local, 4/8/12-byte struct by value, reference to a temporary, non-POD class) either moved it to a register or kept a separate slot. Third: m5a4(m5a0) is folded to the constant 0x3000 by my compile while the target re-reads [this+0x5A0] (0x4FD71C), and the m4e4 Vec3 copy is split as ldm{2}+ldr in the target but as 3 ldr/3 str in mine. Fourth: the 20 x {0,0,1.0f} block at +0x658 is straight-line code in the target (60 stores, no loop), so it is modelled as 20 explicit initialisations inside Sub658's inline ctor; armcc does not unroll a 20-iteration loop here.
helped: The shared headers helped exactly as hoped for the small types: vec3.h's Vec3 (copy-initialised from a global const Vec3) reproduced the target's 14 ldm/stm block copies with no change, and albw_types.h covered the scalars, so no shared header needed editing. The reference Player ctor 0x1DEA54 was the single most useful artefact: its ActorBase/ActorBaseA/ActorBaseB split (0x40C bytes, 21 primary slots, secondary vptr at +0x320) transferred unchanged, and its `new (nt) X()` + init-list idiom is what the target uses throughout. Where the time went: (1) recovering the 0x8BC-byte layout from ~400 stores, now fully documented in actor_types.h and validated by sizeof(EnemyBase) == 0x8BC, which is exactly where the derived ctors (0x206FBC, 0x22141C) put their StateMgr; (2) discovering that 0x5A8..0x657 is one sub-object (the inline list insert addresses [r6+0x54]/[r6+0xa9] with r6 = this+0x5A8, and func_004FC798 uses the same base), which turned a this-relative mess into correct base-relative code; (3) a long tail of armcc code-shape experiments (nothrow tag size, 20-element unrolling, struct-by-value argument placement, bit-test idioms, float-zero vs global-vector initialisation) that each fixed a few instructions - the float-zero fix moved the modulo-register match from 53.2% to 55.9%, and passing the m2d0 index through a local (`s32 idx = 0;`) instead of a literal made armcc materialise it in r5 exactly like the target (0x4FDC74 mov r5,#0) and lifted both metrics again, to 56.7% / 61 exact words - but never the allocator's choice of fp vs sb, which is what keeps the exact-word count low even though the structure is right.
